# Results -- Study 223 (Same-Month Seasonality) on real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: at each
month-end, rank large-cap stocks by their average historical return in the
*next* calendar month (Heston & Sadka 2008); long the top decile (historically
strong in the coming month), short the bottom decile; hold 1 month and
rebalance. Pinned against a random-portfolio control of the same decile size.
**Survivorship-biased**: the universe is a fixed large-cap basket of current
survivors projected backwards -- all results are upper bounds.
As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (last row) |
|--------|--------|-------|----------------------|
| yfinance monthly (adj close) | 1993-01-31 -> 2026-06-30 | 402 months x 85 tickers | `3e4dab6b57ab` |

Universe: ~80 stocks with valid signal in any given month; ~8 in each decile.

## Primary specification (top-minus-bottom decile, 1-month hold)

| Portfolio | Mean return | Vol (ann) | HAC *t* | Ann. Sharpe |
|-----------|------------|-----------|---------|-------------|
| **Top decile (high seasonality)** | **+31.6%/yr** | 24.6% | **+7.86** | **+1.28** |
| Bottom decile (low seasonality)  | +13.9%/yr     | 19.8% | +3.86     | +0.70     |
| Equal-weight market               | +15.3%/yr     | --    | --        | --        |
| **Spread (top - bottom)** | **+17.7%/yr = +147.5 bps/mo** | -- | **+5.57** | -- |
| Top excess over market | +16.2%/yr | -- | +7.46 | -- |

- The top-minus-bottom **spread HAC *t* = +5.57** -- **highly significant**, but this
  is a **survivorship-biased upper bound** on ~8 stocks per decile.
- The block-bootstrap 95% CI on the **spread Sharpe (ann): [+0.56, +1.20]** (0% of
  resamples negative) -- CI fully above zero.
- The random-portfolio null is centred at zero (+0.4 bps/mo mean across 200 draws per
  month), confirming the signal carries genuine cross-sectional information on this panel.

**Critical caveat -- concentration and small n**: with only ~80 stocks in the
universe and a 10% decile, each leg holds roughly **8 stocks**.  At this size,
idiosyncratic noise within the decile is extreme.  In a live, broader universe
(e.g. Russell 1000) the t-stat would fall substantially.

## Sub-period analysis -- persistence check

| Period | Spread/yr | HAC *t* | n months |
|--------|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1999--2008 | +21.0%/yr | **+3.92** | 120 |
| 2009--2017 | +17.0%/yr | **+3.65** | 108 |
| 2018--2026 | +14.1%/yr | **+2.15** | 101 |

The spread is present across all three sub-periods, though it has decayed over
time -- consistent with post-publication arbitrage.  The most recent period
(2018-2026) barely clears t = 2 on the survivorship-biased panel.

Within-month t-stats are low (n~28 per month), but July and December show the
strongest effects.  August and November show negative (but insignificant)
spreads -- the signal reverses in some months.

## Tradability -- turnover and cost drag

The top-decile composition turns over heavily each month: roughly **78%**
average monthly turnover (8 out of 10 stocks change each month).

| One-way cost | Monthly drag | Net spread | Net *t* |
|-------------|-------------|------------|---------|
| 10 bps | **15.7 bps/mo** | +131.9 bps/mo = +15.8%/yr | **+4.98** |
| 20 bps | 31.4 bps/mo | +116.1 bps/mo = +13.9%/yr | +4.38 |

Even at 20 bps one-way, the net spread remains large -- but this masks the
real tradability problem: **8 stocks per decile** means the strategy is
effectively a handful of individual names, not a diversified factor portfolio.
Shorting the bottom decile (8 illiquid distressed names) is costly beyond
simple commission.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds seasonality when planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) the same decile
engine recovers the planted seasonal signal monotonically:

| Planted premium | Spread mean/mo | Spread t-stat |
|----------------|---------------|--------------|
| 0.00 (null)    | ~0% (by chance) | ~0-3 (null) |
| +0.02          | ~+4.7%         | ~+19.6       |
| +0.04          | ~+11.7%        | ~+45.7       |

The engine works; the real tape carries a signal that clears the inference bar
on the survivorship-biased panel but is heavily inflated by concentration and
survivor selection.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- REAL.** Spread HAC *t* = +5.57; bootstrap spread Sharpe CI
  fully above zero.  The signal is stable across all three sub-periods.
  However: (1) the universe is only ~80 names, yielding ~8 per decile --
  an unrealistically concentrated live book; (2) the panel is survivorship-
  biased (current large-cap survivors only); (3) the most recent sub-period
  (2018-2026) drops to t = 2.15.  The effect is academically real but
  significantly overstated on this panel.  Verdict: **REAL**.
- **Tradability -- FRAGILE.** Monthly turnover ~78% on 8-stock deciles; the
  short leg (bottom decile) is similarly concentrated with potential borrow
  costs.  A live implementation on the full Russell 1000 (100+ per decile)
  would face much lower per-stock turnover but also a weaker net signal.
  The survivorship-biased gross spread (+17.7%/yr) is an upper bound; a
  realistic live-trading estimate is substantially lower.  Verdict: **FRAGILE**.
- **Survivorship -- named.**  All results are upper bounds on the actual
  live-universe effect.  The true effect in a broad, delisting-inclusive
  universe is materially weaker.
